abstract: Stringent climate policies have significantly impacted corporate operations and asset values, subjecting companies to increased pressure regarding environmental and social responsibilities, which may lead to the adoption of disingenuous greenwashing practices. Utilizing data from 1219 listed companies on China's A-share market from 2011 to 2022, this study investigates the relationship between stringent climate policies and corporate greenwashing behavior. The findings of this paper are as follows: First, there is a significant positive correlation between stringent climate policies and corporate greenwashing behavior, which has been validated through robustness tests; second, the impact of climate policy on corporate greenwashing exhibits heterogeneity. Enterprises located in the western and eastern regions, those with insufficient technological content, labor-intensive, and highly polluting companies have a greater incentive to engage in greenwashing activities; finally, this study confirms the transmission pathways of internal financial distress and external environmental subsidies as climate risks contributing to corporate greenwashing. This paper holds certain reference value for the government in establishing and improving mechanisms for identifying corporate greenwashing behavior, setting corporate conduct standards, and perfecting the corresponding regulatory system.
